claims.text: A modest increase in Al content destabilizes the predominantly FCC microstructure of Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
The Al-induced FCC destabilization is mediated by changes in electronic structure.
Increasing Al promotes local chemical short-range order in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni.
A modest Al increase produces a fine, uniformly distributed BCC phase within the FCC matrix.
The resulting FCC+BCC microstructure is metastable.
The metastable dual-phase microstructure underpins high-temperature strength.
The metastable dual-phase microstructure underpins environmental resistance.
The metastable dual-phase microstructure underpins radiation tolerance.
The metastable dual-phase microstructure underpins cryogenic toughness.
The baseline Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy has an Al concentration known to produce a predominantly FCC microstructure.
BCC precipitates enhance resistance to shear.
BCC precipitates enhance resistance to radiation-induced defects.
Dispersing BCC precipitates in an FCC matrix preserves cryogenic toughness.
Adding approximately 2 at.% Al will measurably increase the BCC phase fraction relative to the baseline.
The increased BCC fraction will correlate with increased high-temperature yield strength.
The increased BCC fraction will correlate with reduced accumulation of radiation-induced defects.
The increased BCC fraction will maintain or enhance cryogenic toughness.
The proposed behavior holds only over a narrow Al range that nucleates BCC without causing complete phase transformation or overall microstructural destabilization.
Processing history can alter phase development and property outcomes.

contradictions.description: Increasing Al by 2 at.% while keeping the atomic-percent levels of Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni constant is compositionally impossible after normalization; the hypothesis does not state how the other elements are to be reduced or ratio-preserved.
The prediction permits cryogenic toughness merely to be maintained, whereas the falsification rule treats failure to observe an improvement in cryogenic toughness as falsifying.
